questions.question:
What is the appropriate priority (ascending) order of the following?

1. Panchayat Samiti

2. Gram Sabha

3. District Council
questions.solution:
The appropriate priority order is as follows: Gram Sabha< Panchayat Samiti< District Council.

**Gram Sabha: **A gram panchayat (village council) is the only grassroots-level of panchayati raj formalised local self-governance system in India at the village or small-town level, and has a sarpanch as its elected head.

**Panchayat Samiti:** Mandals, taluka panchayats, block panchayats, or panchayat samiti are rural local governments (panchayats) at the intermediate level in panchayat raj institutions (PRI).

**District Council:** The Zila Panchayat or District Council or Zilla Parishad or District Panchayat, is the third tier of the Panchayati Raj system.

questions.question: The concept “creamy layer” refers to ______.

options.text: Classification based on the level of education
None of the option is correct

questions.solution:
• Creamy layer is a term used in Indian politics to refer to the relatively forward and better educated members of the Other Backward Classes (OBCs) who are not eligible for government-sponsored educational and professional benefit programs.
 
• The term was introduced by the Sattanathan Commission in 1971, which directed that the "creamy layer" should be excluded from the reservations (quotas) of civil posts.
 
• The creamy layer (income) criteria is defined as annual family income from all sources more than Rs. 8 lakh (2017).

questions.question: According to the Indian Constitution, who is the head of the executive?

options.text: Cabinet Secretary of Government of India

questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is President.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **As per Article 53 (1) of the Indian Constitution, the head of the executive is the President of India. **
 
• He has **all the constitutional powers and can exercise them directly or through subordinate officers.**
 
• He is, however, only a Constitutional Head of State acting on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers and as such only the formal Executive.
 
• Also, the **President works on the suggestions by the PM.**
 
• The term 'Executive' has been defined both in its broad and narrow forms.
 
• In its broad form, it is taken to mean all the functionaries, political power-holders (Political Executive), and permanent civil servants who undertake the execution of laws and policies and run the administration of the state.

questions.question: Who is known as the father of “Civil Services” in India?
questions.solution:
• Warren Hastings laid the foundation of civil service and **Charles Cornwallis reformed**, **modernized and rationalized** it. Hence, **Charles Cornwallis** is known as the **'Father of Civil Service in India'**.
 
• He introduced Covenanted Civil Services (Higher Civil Services) and Uncovenanted Civil Services (Lower Civil Services).

 
 

 
 
 Lord Cornwallis

 
 
 
Charles Cornwallis, 1st Marquess Cornwallis KG, PC, styled Viscount Brome between 1753 and 1762 and known as Earl Cornwallis between 1762 and 1792, was a British Army general and official.

 
 
 

 
 
 Lord William Bentinck

 
 
 
Lieutenant-General Lord William Henry Cavendish-Bentinck, known as Lord William Bentinck, was a British soldier and statesman. He served as Governor-General of India from 1828 to 1835.

 
 
 

 
 
 Lord Charles Metcalfe

 
 
 
Charles Theophilus Metcalfe, known as Sir Charles Metcalfe, Bt between 1822 and 1845, was a British colonial administrator.

 
 
 

 
 
 Sir Henry Hardinge

 
 
 
Field Marshal Henry Hardinge was a British Army officer and politician. After serving in the Peninsular War and the Waterloo Campaign he became Secretary at War in Wellington's ministry.

questions.question: Who was the last ruler of the Mauryan dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brihadratha**__.

__
 
• Brihadratha Maurya was the last ruler of the Mauryan dynasty.
 
• He was killed by his own general, Pushyamitra Shunga, who later established the Shunga empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mauryan Empire was established by Chandragupta Maurya** by Defeating Dhanananda of the Nanda Dynasty** during 322-21 BC.**
 
• **Mauryan Period (322 BC- 185 BC) **was **one of the most important periods** of **Ancient Indian History**. The literary sources related to this period were **Kautilya"s Arthasastra, Megasthenese's 'Indica', and Visakha Datta's 'Mudra Rakshasa'.**
 
• Buddhist Literature text **Jatakas **( a part of Khuddaknikaya of Suttapitaka which describes 549 stories of Buddha's previous births ) reveals the **general picture of socio-economic conditions** of the **Mauryan period.**

questions.question: What is the main purpose of inclusion of Directive Principles in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
Directive principles are guidelines or directions set for framing of policies and passing of laws by the government.

These guidelines are based on the fundamental rights stated in the Constitution and thus help to establish and maintain socio-economic democracy.

questions.question: Which of the following crops are grown in group during Rabi season in India?
questions.solution:
• There are 3 major crop seasons in India, which are Rabi, Kharif, and Zaid.
 
• The crops grown in the Rabi season include wheat, mustard, and gram. The Rabi crops are sown between October and December and harvested in the month of April and May.
 
• Kharif crops are sown in the monsoon in June and July and harvested in September and October. rice, jowar, cotton, maize are kharif crops
 
• Zaid crops are sown in the summer season, which includes rice, maize, groundnut, and vegetables.

questions.concept: Laws and Principles , Newton's Laws of Motion
questions.question: Newton’s first law is also known as _______.

options.text: None of the option is correct

questions.solution:
There are three Newton’s laws of motion.

__
 
• Newton’s first law is also known as **the law of inertia**__. It states that ‘an object will continue to stay at rest and an object in motion will remain in motion in the same direction and speed unless an unbalanced force acts upon it’.
 
• Newton’s second law of motion states that ‘for a constant mass, force is equal to the product of mass and acceleration. Force is also equal to the change in momentum per change in time.
 
• Newton’s third law of motion states that ‘for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.

questions.question: The lens that collects the rays is called _______ lens.
questions.solution:
• The lens that collects the rays is called a converging or convex lens.
 
• A concave lens is a diverging lens since it causes the beam of parallel light rays to diverge after refraction.
 
• Plano lens is an eyeglass lens that provides no vision correction.
 
• Meniscus lens is concave-convex lens.

questions.question: On which of the following principles does a fuse work?

options.text: On the mechanical effect of electricity
On the magnetic effect of electricity
On the chemical effects of electricity
On the thermal effects of electricity

questions.solution:
• A fuse is a low resistance wire which works on the principle of the thermal effect of electricity.
 
• As soon as the current exceeds a particular limit, the fuse wire melts and cuts-off the supply due to which excessive amount of current is prevented to enter the system.

questions.question: When the volume of a gas is reduced on constant heat, its pressure ________.
questions.solution: When the volume of a gas is reduced on constant heat, its pressure increases and vice versa. This relationship between volume and pressure is known as the Boyle’s law.
